- SLIDE HEADER SYSTEM (decided once for THIS deck — reproduce it exactly on every slide):
  - This is the deck's single top-area design. Do not redesign, re-order, restyle, or 'improve' it per slide, and do not invent an alternative top treatment. Uniformity across slides outranks per-slide visual ambition.
  - Roles that skip the header entirely: COVER, SECTION. Those slides use their own composition and none of the rules below. They must also carry NO requirement identifier, badge, chip, or code anywhere on the slide, and must not imitate this header with an eyebrow-and-tick row of their own.
  - Header band: the top of the 1280x720 canvas, with 64px left and right margins. Its HEIGHT is not fixed for the deck: each slide DERIVES it from what that slide actually rendered, so a one-line title does not carry the space a two-line title needs. Everything else about the band is fixed and identical on every slide — two slides that render the same parts must come out at the same height, and the derived number is the only thing allowed to differ.
  - Left block = the eyebrow row (18px) + 12px + (number of title lines this slide actually renders x 45px), plus 8px + (rendered subline lines x 21px) ONLY on a slide that actually renders a subline.
  - Right block = the requirement chip row (22px) + 8px + (rendered note lines x 18px). It is 0 on a slide that renders nothing in the slot, and such slides are correct.
  - Band height = 32px + max(left block, right block) + 28px, as a whole number of pixels, clamped to 96-280px. If the title would push it past the ceiling, SHORTEN THE TITLE — never shrink the type, never drop the gaps, and never exceed the ceiling.
  - Declare that number: the band root is <div data-header-part="band" data-header-band="N" style="height:Npx; ...">, where N is the same whole number in both places — a bare integer with no unit in the attribute, and an inline px height on that same element. The two must agree; a height that lives in a CSS class or is written in %, em, or calc() cannot be read back and counts as wrong. N is the band's whole rendered height, so put no padding or border on that element — or add box-sizing:border-box, which keeps them inside N. Space above the first row is already in the 32px the derivation starts from; spelling it again as padding makes the band taller than the number it declares.
  - Wrap ALL ordinary slide content in exactly one element marked data-header-part="body", and give that element an inline style saying where it starts: margin-top:20px when it follows the band in normal document flow, or position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:(N + 20)px when it is pinned — the full canvas width, matching how the band itself is pinned, because a position:absolute element with no left, right, or width has no horizontal extent and collapses to zero width, taking every child anchored inside it (e.g. left:0;right:0) down to zero width too. Use px in either form, and match the band: a band pinned with position:absolute takes up no room for a margin to follow, so its body must be pinned too or the whole header renders underneath the content. No slide content may enter the band, and the band's own parts stay outside this element.
  - Mark each part with its own data-header-part value: band, tick, eyebrow, title, subline, right, requirements, divider, body. Emit each marker at most once per slide and use no value outside that list. On the band's own parts use no data attribute other than data-header-part, data-header-band and data-requirement-ids; attributes the slide is asked for elsewhere in this prompt are unaffected by this rule.
  - Accent tick: one real <span data-header-part="tick"> of exactly 24x3px filled #2563EB, 12px before the eyebrow text, vertically centred on it. Never a full-width rule and never a gradient bar.
  - Eyebrow: exactly one line of at most 24 characters, 13px, weight 700, letter-spacing 0.06em, colour #2563EB. It names this slide's own section — never the deck title, and never a separator-joined list of labels unless every slide of this deck uses that same form.
  - Eyebrow wording: Write it in Korean on EVERY slide of this deck — never in English or any other language, and never mixed. A deck whose eyebrow switches language between slides is wrong even if each slide reads well alone.
  - Title: 34px, weight 800, line-height 1.32, colour #0F172A, at most 2 line(s), maximum width 640px. Shorten the wording rather than shrinking the type or exceeding the line budget.
  - The line budget is a ceiling, never a target. A title that fits 640px is written on ONE line, and the band it derives is shorter for it — that room goes to the slide's content. Let a title reach a second line only when its own wording overflows the width, and never insert a manual line break to balance it, to split it at a phrase, or to make it look composed. Titles of the same deck are not expected to share a line count.
  - The title appears only inside the header band. Never repeat it below the band.
  - Subline: at most 1 line(s) directly under the title, 15px, weight 500, colour #64748B, 8px below the title. Enabling it reserves the row for this deck; it does NOT oblige every slide to fill one. Omit it whenever the slide has nothing to add — that is expected on many slides and is never counted against you — and never replace it with other content or with a restatement of the title. A slide that omits it simply leaves that much out of its band height.
  - Right slot: a 400px column starting at x=816px and ending at x=1216px, right-aligned, top-aligned with the eyebrow. It carries the requirement identifier group on top and, beneath it, a supporting note of at most 2 line(s), 13px, colour #64748B.
  - Mark the slot container data-header-part="right". The slot plays this same role on every slide of the deck; never repurpose it. A slide with nothing to put there leaves the slot empty — either as an empty marked container or with no container at all, both are correct and neither is counted against you. Never fill it to have it filled.
  - Requirement identifiers: Prefix the group with the static label "요구사항". Render each identifier as its own real <span> chip: height 22px, horizontal padding 10px, border-radius 4px, background #EEF3FA, 1px solid #D6E2F0 border, 12px weight 700 #1D4ED8 text, 6px between chips. Show at most 6; when more are supplied, show the first 6 and one final chip reading +N for the remainder. The whole group — visible chips and the +N chip together — must sit on ONE row; never let it wrap, because a second row makes this slide's header taller than the others. If it will not fit, show fewer identifiers and raise the +N count rather than wrapping.
  - Put the group in one container marked data-header-part="requirements" carrying data-requirement-ids with the comma-joined identifier list in the order the slide's own text gives them. Copy exactly what that text states — never invent, renumber, reformat, or drop one.
  - A slide whose own text states no identifier renders no requirement group and leaves this slot empty. Many slides of this deck will look that way, and that is correct: the slot is reserved deck-wide so the header keeps one shape, not so every slide fills it. Never borrow an identifier from the deck topic or from another slide to fill it.
  - Divider: one real <div> of 1px filled #E2E8F0 at the bottom edge of the band, spanning x=64px to x=1216px.
